record.field: List the Odoo models the AI is allowed to query. Returns model technical name, business name, and capabilities. Call this when you need to discover what data is available in this Odoo instance. ALWAYS call this if you don't know which model holds the data you need.

Get the full field schema and business semantics for one Odoo model. Returns: field name, type, help text, selection values, relations. Use this BEFORE building a domain or aggregating, to confirm exact field names and field types. Don't guess field names — call this.
List all business relationships involving a given Odoo model — what other models it links to and how. Use this to understand how to traverse data (e.g. sale.order → res.partner → invoices).

Search Odoo records and read specific fields. Returns a list of records. Use this for listing/showing actual records (e.g. "show me overdue invoices", "list our top 10 customers"). Always specify limit. Use 'order' parameter to sort. Domain follows Odoo polish notation: triples of [field, operator, value], with '&' '|' '!' as prefix operators. Allowed operators: =, !=, >, >=, <, <=, in, not in, ilike, like, child_of.
Count records matching a domain. Use this for "how many" questions (orders, invoices, customers, etc.) — it's faster and cheaper than fetching all records and counting.

Compute sum/avg/min/max/count over records matching a domain. Use this for ALL numeric questions: "total sales", "average margin", "total receivables". Returns the scalar value. Cheaper than fetching all records.

Group records and compute aggregates per group. Use this for breakdowns: "sales by salesperson", "invoices by customer", "orders per month". The 'groupby' parameter can include time qualifiers (e.g. "date_order:month"). aggregate_fields is a list of "field:operator" strings; pass "__count" to get just record counts per group.
Read the fields of one specific Odoo record by ID. Use when you already know the record ID (e.g. from a previous search) and need its details.

Find records by approximate name/display-name match. Returns id + display_name pairs. Use this to look up a record when the user gives you a name like "ACME Corp" or "John Smith" and you need the database ID.
Create one or multiple records on an allowed Odoo model. Uses field-level template restrictions and ACL checks. For safety, run with dry_run first, then execute.
Update records on an allowed model using either record_ids or domain. Enforces ACL + template field controls. Always supports dry_run preview before applying writes.
Delete records on an allowed model by record_ids or domain. High-risk operation. Always run with dry_run first, then apply only after explicit approval.

Call a business method on records (for example action_confirm, action_post, button_validate). Only non-private business methods are allowed. This enables workflow execution similar to button actions in the UI.

List the predefined KPI definitions configured in this system. Each KPI has a code, business meaning, default aggregation, and synonyms. Use this to find a canonical KPI for the user's question before reinventing the calculation via odoo_aggregate.
{"type": "object", "properties": {"category": {"type": "string", "description": "Optional category filter: sales, finance, operations, crm, hr, procurement, inventory, custom."}}, "required": []}

Compute the value of a named KPI using its predefined formula. Prefer this over hand-rolling odoo_aggregate when a KPI definition exists for what the user is asking — the KPI formula encodes the correct business logic.

Compute the 6-domain business health score (liquidity, growth, execution, pipeline, fulfillment, receivables) plus an overall score 0–100 and letter grade. Returns input metrics and early-warning flags. Use this when the user asks about business health, overall status, or risk indicators.
{"type": "object", "properties": {"with_narrative": {"type": "boolean", "description": "If true, also generate an AI narrative analysis (slower)."}}, "required": []}

Project a financial KPI forward using linear-trend regression on the last 12 historical periods. Returns projected values with 95% confidence bands. Use for "what will X be next month / quarter / year" questions.

Simulate the impact of a business change. Returns projected impact per metric vs. current baseline plus a sensitivity table. Use for "what if we…" questions (price changes, volume changes, customer churn, cost changes, headcount changes).

Fetch the latest industry/peer benchmark value for a metric category. Returns median + percentile bands when available. Use this when the user asks how something compares to industry, peers, or the market.

Compare this company's actual metrics to industry benchmarks across multiple categories at once. Returns gap percentages and percentile bands (top quartile, above median, below median, bottom quartile). Use this for comprehensive "how do we compare" answers.
List all attachments (files/documents) on a specific Odoo record. Use this before analyzing a document to find the attachment_id you need.
Extract text and structured data from an attached document (PDF, image, office file). Returns the extracted content. Use when the user asks about the contents of a specific attachment.
Extract tabular/text data from a file attachment (PDF, image OCR, CSV, Excel). Returns the parsed context and table rows so the assistant can reason over document content before import.

Import structured rows from a document attachment into an Odoo model using an explicit field map. Honors Odoo ACLs and access-template field restrictions. Use dry_run first, then execute after approval.
Queue a reminder for the current user. Goes through human approval before execution. Use when the user asks you to remind them about something.
Queue creation of a follow-up activity on an Odoo record. Goes through approval. Use when the user asks to "create a task", "schedule a follow-up", "assign work" on a specific record.
Queue a message to be posted on a record's chatter. Goes through approval. Use when the user asks you to "post a note", "leave a comment", "notify on chatter".

Run the configured validation rules against an Odoo record and return what's missing or invalid. Read-only — does not mutate. Use when the user asks "is this record OK?", "validate this", or "check this".
